correctness.rationale: For n>=2 the source Corollary 4.1/Definition 4.2 gives primitive cone rays. The lower-unitriangular second-difference lattice automorphism sends rho_(n-j) to basis f_(j+1), old e_j to f_j−2f_(j+1)+f_(j+2), and u to −f_1+f_2. A one in the binary cone forces z_(i+1)=0; a zero forces a second-difference relation, with terminal z_(n+1)=0. Each interval between forced zeros contributes exactly one independent generator w with g*w=0; the all-zero word gives trivial quotient. Thus N/N_sigma=⊕Z/g and its finite Smith invariants agree with local toric Cl for full-dimensional simplicial cones. Maximizing the gap product means i_1=0 and an ordered composition of n; replacing 1 and >=5, and three 2s, derives standard 3/2 integer break. Counts are 1 for n=3a, a+1 for n=3a+2, and a(a+3)/2 for n=3a+1. Independent sympy Smith normal forms and determinants on all 508 cones of 2<=n<=8 confirmed every cyclic-factor profile, maximum and multiplicity. This is not a universal computational proof: the recurrence and integer-break argument is.

originality.rationale: The full fixed-point group spectrum is a direct special case of Arena–Song’s published §7 boundary-stratum quotient and stabilizer rule, together with its own primitive toric stack fan and the general inertia/class-group identification from Goldin et al. and toric divisor theory. The binary-gap code is exactly the ordered composition of bubble lengths; at each bubble’s unique torus-fixed point the nonzero highest elementary symmetric coordinate forces stabilizer μ_g. Its character group gives Z/g. Ordered integer compositions yield the claimed sharp maximum and counts by the standard integer-break argument; no genuinely original substantive remainder survived. Different naming and absence of verbatim formula do not avoid prior implication.
residual_risks: No uncertainty about the key prior implication: the Arena–Song §7 product formula combined with their primitive-ray toric stack and standard inertia/class-group identification covers the complete fixed-point group spectrum.

The primary paper does not print the displayed integer-break maximizer counts verbatim; they follow from already covered bubble sizes via an elementary ordered-composition count and do not save the overall originality claim.

The explicit second-difference Smith presentation is a useful alternate proof but mathematically equivalent to the earlier inertia computation for these fixed cones; independent novelty for that technique was not shown.
The comparison is for the coarse toric fixed points over C, not a claim about nonfixed-orbit local classes or analytic singularity types.
Finite Smith-normal-form tests n=2..8 do not replace the universal proof.
